procedural_matters: GBR 1556 did not come to the hearing. The jury started the hearing under RRS 62.1(b).
GBR 1556 gave a good reason for arriving late, and so the jury restarted the hearing with GBR 1556 present.
Andrew Russell gave evidence as a witness.
facts: During Race 1 of the RS 400 fleet, the conditions were 12 knots of breeze and 1 meter waves. Boat speed in these conditions is about 5 knots.
GBR 1456 entered the zone on a close-hauled starboard tack and fetching the windward mark.
GBR 1456 was overlapped to leeward of the port aft quarter of GBR 1272 by 30cm, with a lateral distance of 60cm.
GBR 1556 was on a close-hauled port tack on a converging course with GBR 1456 and GBR 1272.
One meter before the mark, GBR 1556 passed head to wind and reached a close-hauled starboard course, one meter in front of GBR 1456.
Immediately after, GBR 1456 luffed above close-hauled, and made contact with the port aft quarter of GBR 1272.
After rounding the mark, GBR 1272 took a 1-turn penalty.
GBR 1556 did not take a penalty turn.
There was no damage or injury.
conclusions: GBR 1556 caused GBR 1456, who was on starboard tack since entering the zone, to sail above close-hauled to avoid contact with GBR 1556. GBR 1556 broke RRS 18.3(a).
GBR 1556 caused contact between GBR 1456 and GBR 1272 even though it was reasonably possible to avoid causing it, and broke RRS 14(b).
It was not reasonably possible for GBR 1456, the right-of-way boat, to avoid contact with GBR
GBR 1272 to windward failed to keep clear of GBR 1456 to leeward, and broke RRS 1 1.
Since GBR 1272 was compelled to break RRS 11 as a consequence of GBR 1556 breaking RRS 18.3(a), she is exonerated under RRS 43.1(a) for this breach.
